subject: Post-call: Private connectivity clarifications & egress IPs
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
To: Kerry Malone <kerry@finops.inc>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Nov 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Private connectivity clarifications & egress IPs

Hi Kerry — thanks for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and a short list of asks so we can size the Private VPC work and lock in next steps.

Call highlights (very brief)
- FinOps wants the Redwood runtime in a Private VPC in us-west-2.
- Security leans toward PrivateLink for control plane + management traffic, but infra team is evaluating VPC peering for data-plane throughput from their EKS clusters.
- Procurement needs an estimated lead time and any static IP ranges for firewall allowlists.

Items we need from you to progress the technical qualification:
1) Connectivity preference: Please confirm whether you want to pursue PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink) only, VPC peering only, or a hybrid approach (control plane PrivateLink + peering for data). If hybrid, please indicate which workloads would use peering.
2) Egress / SNAT IPs: We will provide a minimal set of static egress IPs (recommended: /29) for your allowlist. Can you confirm the aggressive/strictness of your allowlist (single /29 OK, or do you require a /28)? Also confirm the expected number of outbound flows concurrently (approx requests/sec) so we can size NAT Gateway/pools.
3) Transit/Shared services: Do you use a Transit Gateway or centralized shared-services VPC (we need to know whether route propagation is allowed or if we should plan for explicit routes)?
4) BGP / peering details: If you opt for VPC peering over a Direct Connect/Edge, do you require us to advertise any ASN or accept BGP? If so, please provide the ASN and any prefix limits.
5) TLS inspection / proxy: Does your infra impose TLS inspection or an egress proxy that requires custom CA or SNI passthrough?
6) Compliance artifacts: For your security review, we can attach our Private VPC checklist and IP ranges document (attached draft). Tell us where to upload final artifacts (Secure Drive, Confluence, or direct to procurement email).

Attachments: network-canvas.png (high-level topology), redwood_private_vpc_requirements.pdf (draft checklist)

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm items 1–5 above by EOD Fri 11/10.
- If PrivateLink is the path, we will schedule a 30-min technical session (Ben) to walk the network ops team through DNS, endpoint policy, and mTLS if needed.
- If peering is chosen, we will prepare a peering plan with route tables and required allowlist prefixes.

Can you confirm preferred path and someone on your netops side we should loop in (cced networkops@finops.inc if possible)?

Thanks — happy to be concise here and iterate.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.ai

From: Kerry Malone <kerry@finops.inc>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>
Cc: networkops@finops.inc
Date: Thu, 09 Nov 2028 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Private connectivity clarifications & egress IPs

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear recap. Below are answers from our side; I've looped in networkops as requested.

Answers:
1) Preference: Security team prefers AWS PrivateLink for anything that touches customer data (control plane + admin APIs). For high-throughput model traffic from our EKS clusters, we are leaning toward VPC peering to avoid added hop latency. We are OK with a hybrid approach: PrivateLink for control, peering for data.
2) Egress/SNAT: We require a static set of egress IPs for our firewall allowlist. /29 is preferred; we could accept a /28 if justified. Expected concurrent outbound flows: approx 800–1,200 rps during peak for the feature flagged rollout.
3) Transit: We use a Transit Gateway in us-west-2. Route propagation is allowed but must be reviewed by our netops.
4) BGP: We do not expect you to run BGP; peering will be standard VPC peering. If Direct Connect is used later, we can revisit ASN exchange.
5) TLS inspection: We do not perform TLS inspection on egress traffic (no custom interception), but our internal proxy requires SNI passthrough and does whitelist SNI.
6) Artifacts: Please upload final artifacts to our S3 share (I'll DM a presigned link to networkops), and send procurement a copy (procurement@finops.inc).

Timeline: procurement aims for a security review window the week of 11/20. If you can provide allowlist IPs and topology by 11/14 we can include it in the packet.

I've attached our internal network policy spreadsheet with CIDR limits and port restrictions.

Kerry
Kerry Malone
Head of Infrastructure, FinOps Inc
kerry@finops.inc

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kerry Malone <kerry@finops.inc>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Nov 2028 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Private connectivity clarifications & egress IPs

Kerry — thanks for the fast answers and for attaching the policy. A few technical clarifications from our infra side so we can produce the right artifacts:

- Egress IP sizing: we can allocate a /29 (8 IPs) for outbound SNAT per tenant; if you need /28 we can provide that but it requires additional provisioning lead time. Please confirm preference.
- Ports and protocols: we plan to use outbound 443 for TLS model traffic. Do you have any port-level restrictions beyond 443 (e.g., health probes, metrics, tracing endpoints on high ports)?
- Hostname/ SNI: For PrivateLink we will create interface endpoints with DNS names. You mentioned SNI whitelisting — will your proxy allow wildcard SNI entries (e.g., *.redwood-inference.internal) or do you need explicit FQDNs per endpoint?
- MTU & packet shape: If you route via Transit Gateway, do you enforce a lower MTU (we've seen 1,400 bytes in some shared infra setups). If so, we need to tune our gRPC chunking/keepalive config.
- Route scope: For peering, do you need explicit route table entries for each subnet or will CIDR-based propagation be sufficient?

Actionable asks for your team:
- Confirm SNAT prefix (/29 vs /28) and provide preferred public IP owner name for the allowlist.
- Confirm whether wildcard SNI is acceptable or list required FQDNs.
- Share any additional port restrictions (besides 443) and expected allowed destination IPs for observability callbacks (we use a handful of telemetry endpoints for metrics/logs).

Once we have these items we will: (a) produce a short peering diagram and route table draft, (b) list the egress IPs, and (c) schedule a 30-minute network ops call for next week (Ben + your netops).

FWIW: We can stand up the PrivateLink endpoints sooner (2–3 business days) once you confirm TLS/SNI expectations and the DNS handling. Peering plan usually takes ~5–7 business days for prep + IP table reviews.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call: Private connectivity clarifications & egress IPs — action list & next steps

Kerry / NetOps — thanks for the quick replies and the spreadsheet. Recap of agreed items and owners below so nothing slips:

Agreed approach:
- Hybrid deployment: PrivateLink for control plane + VPC peering for data-plane (EKS) traffic.

Open items & owners (please confirm dates):
1) SNAT prefix size — Kerry / FinOps to confirm whether /29 is sufficient or /28 required (requested by 2028-11-14).
2) SNI wildcard vs explicit FQDN — Kerry / NetOps to confirm preferenced SNI handling (2028-11-14).
3) Port list & telemetry endpoints — FinOps to confirm any non-443 rules and allowed observability IPs (2028-11-14).
4) Governance & artifacts — Sofia to upload final Private VPC checklist and peering diagram to the S3 share once provided; procurement@finops.inc to be copied.
5) Technical call — Ben to host a 30-min netops session the week of 2028-11-13 (please propose 2x 30-min windows).

Deliverables from Redwood once items above are confirmed:
- Peering diagram & route table draft (PDF)
- Static egress IP list (/29 suggestion)
- PrivateLink endpoint DNS names and expected TLS cert/SNI values
- Quick runbook for failover: if peering is unavailable, traffic will fall back to the hosted gateway (we will document this as part of the A/B rollout).

Next steps: Kerry — please confirm the three items above and reply-all with the S3 presigned link for artifact upload. If the dates work, we'll schedule Ben's technical call and mark in HubSpot (deal D-2028-1123).

Thanks all — looking forward to getting this into the procurement packet.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
